test_title: PYST 14 - SSC CHSL 2025 - General Awareness (Held On: 17 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following pair regarding the parts of the Indian constitution is NOT correctly matched?

options.text: Services Under the Union and the States - Part XIV

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Fundamental Rights - Part III:** The Fundamental Rights are enshrined in **Part III** of the Indian Constitution, covering Articles **12 to 35**. These rights ensure the basic freedoms of citizens. *Hence, this statement is correct.*

• **Panchayats - Part IX:** Part IX of the Constitution, added by the **73rd Amendment Act of 1992**, deals with Panchayati Raj institutions (local self-governance). Articles **243 to 243-O** provide constitutional recognition to Panchayats. *Hence, this statement is correct.*

• **Elections - Part XV:** Elections in India are governed by **Part XV** of the Constitution, not Part XVII. Part XV encompasses Articles **324 to 329**, which deal with the election process and the powers of the Election Commission. **Part XVII**, on the other hand, deals with the **Official Languages**. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

• **Services under Union and States - Part XIV:** Part XIV of the Constitution deals with Services under the Union and the States, covering Articles **308 to 323**. It includes provisions for public services and Public Service Commissions. *Hence, this statement is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Fundamental Rights:**

• Fundamental Rights are considered the cornerstone of democracy in India.

• They are enforceable by courts and include rights such as **Right to Equality**, **Right to Freedom**, **Right against Exploitation**, **Right to Freedom of Religion**, **Cultural and Educational Rights**, and **Right to Constitutional Remedies**.

• These rights are applicable to Indian citizens, and some are extended to non-citizens as well.

• **Panchayati Raj System:**

• The system of Panchayati Raj was constitutionally established to decentralize governance.

• The 73rd Amendment Act introduced a three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat, Intermediate Panchayat, and District Panchayat.

• It empowers Panchayats to prepare plans for economic development and social justice.

• **Elections:**

• Elections in India are conducted under the supervision of the **Election Commission**, which is established by Article 324.

• India follows a **first-past-the-post system** for elections to the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.

• The Election Commission ensures free and fair elections, maintains the electoral roll, and regulates political parties.

• **Services under Union and States:**

• The Constitution provides for **All-India Services** such as the IAS, IPS, and IFS, which are common to both the Union and the States.

• State services are governed by respective state public service commissions.

• Provisions ensure impartiality, efficiency, and accountability in public administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Part XV:** This part of the Constitution is crucial for maintaining the democratic structure of the country. It includes provisions for delimitation, preparation of electoral rolls, and qualifications for membership of legislatures.

• **Part XVII:** Official Languages are covered under this part, with provisions for Hindi as the official language and safeguards for linguistic minorities.

• **Evolution of Panchayats:** The concept of Panchayati Raj dates back to the **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee** (1957), which recommended a three-tier system for rural governance.

• **Judiciary and Fundamental Rights:** The judiciary acts as a guardian of Fundamental Rights, ensuring they are upheld against any violation by the state or individuals.
</ul
